text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Antiretroviral therapy with bictegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide once daily, chosen for its high barrier to resistance and few interactions with his cardiac medicines; viral load and CD4 count every three months
  • Infectious diseases consultation to co-manage HIV: the regimen and its interactions, opportunistic-infection prophylaxis, the monitoring schedule, and vaccines
  • Toxoplasma maintenance therapy with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole double strength twice daily, which also prevents Pneumocystis pneumonia, until the CD4 count is above 200 for more than six months on suppressive therapy; blood count, potassium, and creatinine every three months while on it
  • Secondary prevention of coronary disease after two bypass operations: aspirin, high-intensity atorvastatin with ezetimibe added for an LDL goal below 55 mg/dL, blood pressure below 130/80, a heart-healthy diet, regular exercise, and a written chest-pain plan with sublingual nitroglycerin
  • Vaccines for adults with HIV: pneumococcal, hepatitis B with an antibody check afterwards, the two-dose meningococcal ACWY series, recombinant zoster, and seasonal influenza and COVID-19, with no live vaccines while the CD4 count is below 200
  • Person-first, confidential care: he decides who learns of his diagnosis; support with disclosure if and when he chooses, peer support, and depression screening with the PHQ-9 at intake and six months and the PHQ-2 at the preventive visit

resource.title: Arthur Ashe synthetic care plan
resource.description: Person-first, confidential primary care for a 45-year-old man four months after HIV was diagnosed with cerebral toxoplasmosis, who also has coronary artery disease after two bypass operations: viral load and CD4 monitoring on bictegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide (an antiretroviral regimen chosen to avoid interactions with his statin and cardiac medicines and to avoid abacavir), trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole maintenance and its safe discontinuation by CD4 count, vaccines for adults with HIV, and secondary prevention of coronary disease to an LDL goal below 55 mg/dL, on the DHHS and IAS-USA antiretroviral guidance, the DHHS opportunistic infection guidelines, the HIVMA/IDSA primary care guidance, and the CMID ischemic heart disease and hyperlipidemia monographs.
